notes: Every number the engine uses lives in this file with a source. Change a rule here, nowhere else. Items with verify:true must not be shown to judges as facts.

tariffs.source: KSEB LT-1A Domestic tariff table (idea doc section 7, S7). Check against KSEB's online bill calculator.
tariffs.verified_source: kseb.in LT-1 Domestic tariff page, column 01.04.2025 to 31.03.2027: every energy and fixed-charge row matches, including 286/285 for 401-500 units (as published, not a typo)

tariffs.source: kseb.in LT-1 Domestic page, column 05.12.2024 to 31.03.2025
tariffs.verified_source: kseb.in LT-1 Domestic tariff page, column 05.12.2024 to 31.03.2025

billing.verify: Two-month bills: slabs are applied to units/2 per month, then scaled (idea doc 5.2). Confirm on KSEB's calculator.

tod_domestic.source: kseb.in LT-1 Domestic page, ToD note: 90% of the ruling tariff 06-18 h, 125% 18-22 h, 100% 22-06 h; applies to homes whose average monthly use is above 500 units (ToD meter needed)

bill_extras.source: kseb.in FAQ: Electricity Duty = 10% of Energy Charge
bill_extras.not_included: meter rent and the fuel surcharge change from bill to bill and are not modelled

bill_check.source: idea doc section 6: warn if the amount differs from our own tariff calculation by over 20%
bill_check.verify: Expected = energy + fixed charge + 10% duty. Meter rent and the fuel surcharge are not modelled, so real bills can run a little higher. Tune the tolerance on the 3 real bills.

pm_surya_ghar.source: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (S11)
pm_surya_ghar.verify: Subsidy amounts (30,000 per kW to 2 kW, 18,000 for the third kW, cap 78,000) were confirmed on government pages (Delhi solar portal, Pune) on 2026-10-24. The 31 Mar 2027 end date is NOT confirmed and the official portal could not be read: check pmsuryaghar.gov.in for the deadline and any extension.

net_metering.cap_note: KSERC Renewable Energy and Related Matters Regulations 2025 (notified, in force 2025-11-06): reports on the draft say net metering is for 1-3 kW (5 kW with 30% storage) and larger systems use net billing. The idea doc says 1-20 kW. For systems above 3 kW the savings here may be too high until the notified text is checked.
net_metering.source: KSERC net-metering rules in force from 2025-11-06 (S9, S10)
net_metering.verify: Notified regulations are in force from 2025-11-06 (billing changes from 2026-01-01), but the net-metering size limit (3 kW per draft reports vs 20 kW in the idea doc), the 2.79 surplus rate (draft reports: 75% of SECI FY25 bid for new systems) and the 1 rupee grid-support charge on exports were NOT confirmed against the notified text. Check the Kerala Gazette or serckerala.org.

solar.panel_note: ASSUMPTION: 400 Wp panels, only used to turn kW into a panel count

sizing.source: design choice: stop adding panels when the next 0.5 kW takes more than 10 years to pay back (after its extra subsidy). 25-year benefit assumes 0.5% output loss a year.
sizing.verify: Check the 10-year rule and the 0.5% degradation with an installer.

rain.tank_rule: smallest tank beyond which each extra day of stored demand adds under marginal_gain_pp_per_day points of reliability (the knee of the curve)
rain.source: Open-Meteo archive, 10 years of daily rain (2016-2025)

co2.source: CEA CO2 Baseline Database v20.0 (FY 2023-24): weighted average 0.727 tCO2/MWh, as reported by SolarQuarter and Climatiq
co2.verify: CEA has newer versions (v21 Nov 2025 for FY 2024-25, v22 Aug 2026 for FY 2025-26): open the User Guide on cea.nic.in and replace 0.727 with the latest weighted average.

home_defaults.verify: Replace with the survey median once Kishan has real answers.

public_building.source: assumption: about 3 storeys, 5 kWh per m2 of floor per month
public_building.verify: Replace with the campus's real monthly units (ask the college office). PM Surya Ghar and the domestic tariff do not apply to public buildings.

typical_kerala.source: Sun: NASA POWER climatology at Pozhiyoor (8.30N, 77.09E). Rain: rough Kerala-wide monthly normals. Last-resort fallback only, when no cached or live data exists.
typical_kerala.verify: Fallback only. Flagged as quality.data = typical in every response.

kerala.source: 3.37 lakh solar homes under PM Surya Ghar (idea doc S12); record peak about 6,195 MW on 23 Apr 2026 (news reports)
kerala.verify: The 3.37 lakh figure comes from the idea doc: confirm its source. The 2 units moved per home per day is our assumption.

ward.source: assumption: Kerala homes are a mix of flat concrete (0.50 usable) and sloped (0.40 usable) roofs
ward.verify: Replace with survey data on roof types and sizes.

veyil.profile_note: ASSUMPTION: a typical Kerala home profile (30% always-on: fridge, fans, standby; the rest shaped by use through the day). Tuned so a typical home uses about a third of its own solar at home; KSEB reports 36% (S6).
veyil.profile_verify: Replace with smart-meter or survey data if available.

ev_charger.note: ASSUMPTION: a slow home charger adding about 7 kWh (roughly 40 km); only useful if the car is home in the daytime. KSEB asked people to avoid EV charging at peak.
